rendered:
Panel C of Fig. 2[1] shows the mean genome GC content of S. marcescens as μ = 59.74%[2]. A dashed vertical line marks this mean on the histogram, and the distribution peaks near 60.0%[3].

Panel D plots coding GC against intergenic GC. The correlation between them is r = 0.57[4], and it is statistically significant (p < 0.001[5]). The fitted line slopes upward, so this is a moderate positive correlation: coding GC tends to rise as intergenic GC rises.

source.caption: Fig. 2. Phenotypic characteristics and genomic diversity of S. marcescens. (A) Temperature-dependent prodigiosin pigmentation phenotype; (B) distribution of the prodigiosin biosynthetic gene cluster among different biogroups; (C–D) GC content and genomic compositional characteristics; (E) pangenome composition and genomic variability; and (F) predicted host range of plasmids identified in S. marcescens. The figure summarizes the multi-level diversity of S. marcescens in phenotype, genome composition, and genetic plasticity.
